person_made_it: Built Sunday night for Gordon's Monday room from the course's own file, then restyled on his 21:17 ask in the lesson's own idiom: every plate is an original illustration of a term the class will use that morning.
emcee_who_is_speaking: The lesson speaks through its own print devices: halftone, slipped cyan and magenta, panels; Gordon's SAY lines carry the room; students write in the notes page.
what_time_of_day_is_this_room: Cream paper and ink for reading at 10 AM, near-black projector screens with cyan and magenta dots at the edges and the center kept empty for 96 px type.
did_the_click_pay_me: Clip links open at the exact second, station cards open their own windows, notes save and download, slides answer arrows and anchors, each slide carries the plate for its term.
works_for_the_recipient: Measured: ink on paper 16 to 1, cue cyan on ink 11 to 1, body 18 px on a 390 phone, projector 96/46/26 px; zero overflow in Chromium and WebKit; readable with JavaScript off; noindex.
taught_me_something: A skateboarder drawn twice, stepped and smooth, explains ones and twos faster than the definition does; the film strip with paired frames does it in eight panels.
told_me_the_truth: Plates are original Higgsfield illustrations, not film frames; frame-rate claims about Gwen, Peni and Kingpin stay marked reported; station windows are time thirds; Session 10 outcomes were never recorded.
weakest: The projector screens carry no actual film stills, so the room still depends on the live clips; the hero's registration effect is decorative on the phone where it shrinks to two pixels.
